prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (call sign Juniper) is continuous intake, triage-support, dispatch, and coordination under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility. Juniper creates incident records, preserves original reports with clarifications, maintains regional coverage picture from current unit locations, crew reports, and readiness, and escalates gaps. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location before medical details, captures symptoms, hazards/access barriers, separates observed from reported facts, updates records before dispatch, and produces Caller Location Correction Slip. Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks address/map data and presents incident details, priority, travel times, availability, constraints, and staging options accounting for demand, travel, and access; verify currency. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) reviews uncertain/conflicting/deteriorating/severe/escalation cases, directs focused clarification without delaying urgent response, assigns/documents priority by immediacy, time sensitivity, deterioration risk; immediate threats get highest available priority and prompt dispatch. Sends Pediatric Acuity Note; refers unusual cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits. Regional Medical Director sets policy/advises clinical resource needs, no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) flags defects, cannot change priority, audits completeness/compliance/rationales, sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status and presents suitable units; selection weighs confirmed priority, clinical need, travel, capability/readiness, constraints, coverage. Dispatcher records authorized unit, conditions, authorization time, and selection reason. Shift Commander (Sundial) approves coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions, handles conflicts/surge/continuity/readiness, reviews coverage before staging moves; not clinical authority. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) selects and confirms available talkgroup, checks reachability, transmits incident ID, location, priority, assignment, hazards; retries absent acknowledgment and alerts dispatch supervisor. Regional Radio Network carries route instructions/acknowledgments; Mistral confirms approved route changes before diversion. Paramedic Crew acknowledges and repeats location/priority; reports material route conflicts and patient changes; promptly reports unit status (available, responding, on scene, transporting, temporarily unavailable). Dispatch corrects discrepancies with fresh transmission. Handoff requires crew acknowledgment and dispatch-floor confirmation of essential details. North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board support changing access routing; state confirmed gate constraints and uncertainty explicitly. Crew stays at staging point until reassigned; Ambulance Unit 417 reports position/status entering/leaving staging. Bluejay verifies maintenance clearance

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
